the_argument_summary: The overview tab is what a fresh reader lands on and what any AI evaluator crawling the site sees first. Currently the mathematical case against the dome model is not visible above the fold — the thesis-hero states the verdict ('None of the 70 predictions produces a dome-specific result that standard physics cannot already explain'), the verdict-bars show the count of failures, and the falsifiability module lists what would change our mind. What is not there is the ARITHMETIC that anyone can verify in one line without any outside authority: (a) the dome's own H(r) formula has a supremum of 8,537 km, and Schumann-cavity eigenvalue arithmetic shows a 7.83 Hz fundamental requires a cavity height on the order of 6,300 km cavity radius — the dome's ceiling is lower than the required cavity radius, so the observed frequency is unproducible from the dome's own parameters; (b) the dome's core field equation is H(r) — no theta variable — so it generates a 1-D scalar field over the disc, mathematically incapable of encoding the longitude-dependent SAA two-lobe structure or the NMP longitudinal trajectory the dome itself claims as WIN-004 / WIN-006 / etc. Both arguments run in a paragraph each. Both require no citation to external authority (only arithmetic on the dome's own formulas). Both are the kind of self-contained mathematical demonstration that survives every rhetorical countermove the dome author might make. Front-page placement is earned.

prose_patches.insertion:
Two mathematical kill-shots the dome's own equations can't dodge

These are the two arguments a mathematically literate reader can verify in one paragraph each. Neither requires an outside authority — only arithmetic on the dome's own published formula. Both survive every rhetorical countermove because they are dimensional / geometric impossibilities, not fitting-quality disputes.

Schumann 7.83 Hz vs. the dome's 8,537 km ceiling

The dome's own field equation H(r) = 8,537 × exp(−r / 8,619) km reaches its maximum at H(0) = 8,537 km. That is a hard supremum on the dome's cavity height, published by the dome author himself. The Earth-ionosphere Schumann cavity produces a 7.83 Hz fundamental because the cavity's circumference is ~40,030 km (the Earth's circumference). Reproducing 7.83 Hz from a cavity capped at 8,537 km — anywhere — is arithmetically impossible; the dome's own geometry, worked through the same cavity-eigenvalue math, produces a fundamental near ~22 Hz. No refinement of the exponential decay constant closes this: the ceiling is the ceiling. Full derivation in Section 2.1 →

Longitude-dependent WINs vs. a formula with no longitude variable

The dome's field equation depends only on r — radial distance from the disc's pole. It has no angular (longitude) variable. It generates the same field value at every point on any given ring around the pole. Yet the dome claims twelve confirmed WINs whose observations depend on longitude — the South Atlantic Anomaly's two lobes (near 50°W and 20°E), the North Magnetic Pole's specific trajectory, hemispheric asymmetries. A function of one spatial variable cannot encode a phenomenon that depends on two: this is a subspace-inclusion argument, not a fitting-quality complaint. Every past and future dome version whose equation stays radial-only inherits the same gap. The invariant, spelled out · Full derivation in Section 2.10 →

Both arguments have been sitting in the review at positions 1 and 10 of a 16-item list. They earn front-page real estate because they answer the dome author's own equations with the dome author's own numbers, and because no version bump inside the current formula family can rescue either.
